name: Liaodactylus
sum: Earliest known ctenochasmatid and first filter-feeding pterosaur from the Jurassic Yanliao Biota of Liaoning, China.
holotype: PMOL-AP00031 — Tiaojishan Formation, Daxishan, Jianchang County, Liaoning.
material: Complete skull (13.3 cm), lower jaws and first two neck vertebrae.
biology: About 150 long, comb-like interlocking teeth used to filter food; closely related to Ctenochasma.
author: Zhou et al. 2017

species.name: Liaodactylus primus
species.author: Zhou et al. 2017
species.ref: C.-F. Zhou, K.-Q. Gao, and H.-Y. Yi, J.-Z. Xue, Q.-G. Li, R. C. Fox. 2017. Earliest filter-feeding pterosaur from the Jurassic of China and ecological evolution of Pterodactyloidea. Royal Society Open Science 4(160672)
